# Poznań three-way comparison: findings (hand-written; tables in REPORT.md are generated by `make poznan-three-way`)

Status 2026-09-29. Manifest: 200 held-out frames of route IcRzj × 2024/2025 orthophotos (400 entries), crop centred
within ±22 m / ±10° of the Mapillary pose proxy. Decisions and reasoning: docs/decisions.md, 2026-09-29 entries.

## Headline (protocol `prior`: the panorama is oriented by the noisy crop heading, every method recovers the rest)

| Method | Median (95 % CI) | ≤ 10 m | > 30 m | Heading | Trained on Poznań | Job |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loc², UniK3D depth | **3.50 m** (3.26–3.77) | 85 % | 3 % | 2.0° | no | 8854986 |
| Loc², flat-ground depth proxy (1.65 m) | 3.91 m (3.47–4.25) | 83 % | 3 % | 2.3° | no | 8854985 |
| FG² | 4.15 m (3.82–4.56) | 86 % | 0 % | 2.4° | no | 8854984 |
| PanoRoMa two-pass, 71 m imagery extent | **4.53 m** (3.88–5.12) | 76 % | 3 % | 4.2° | no | 8854993 |
| PanoRoMa two-pass, 71 m, scale-free `sim` solver | 4.53 m (3.93–5.20) | 74 % | 3 % | 5.2° | no | 8855335 |
| PanoRoMa two-pass, full 112 m canvas, north-up | 4.75 m (4.03–5.39) | 76 % | 4 % | 4.4° | no | 8854987 |
| PanoRoMa two-pass, crop-up canvas | 5.01 m (4.50–5.57) | 77 % | 3 % | 4.4° | no | 8854992 |
| IPM + Sat-RoMa (earlier method of record) | 5.69 m (4.94–6.54) | 71 % | 5 % | 2.6° | yes, selected on this route | — |

Protocol `gt` (panorama oriented by the true heading, as in the rows first reported in task 02) moves FG² and Loc² by
< 0.2 m (FG² 3.98, Loc² flat 4.01, Loc² UniK3D 3.53 m): the true-heading roll in the old rows barely mattered.

## Readings

1. PanoRoMa transfers: zero-shot from VIGOR it is 1.2 m better than our Poznań-trained IPM matcher, with fewer gross
   misses (3 % vs 5 %).
2. It is still 1.0 m behind Loc² with the same UniK3D depth maps, and its heading error is about twice Loc²'s.
3. Restricting the reference imagery to VIGOR's 71 m tile size helps a little (4.53 vs 4.75 m): PanoRoMa learned on
   71 m tiles with a black border.
4. The pose solver is not the cause: the scale-free 4-DoF solver gives the same 4.53 m.
5. Training budget is not like for like: PanoRoMa ≈ 6 epochs at batch 4; FG² 25 epochs at batch 24; Loc²'s code runs
   up to 100 epochs at batch 80. A 100-epoch PanoRoMa run is being prepared (batch / data-pipeline probe first).
6. The IPM row is not zero-shot and this route is its dev set; route irAsB (`manifest_test.json`) is untouched.

## Depth scale (checked before touching it)

Camera height implied by UniK3D depth, one rule on both datasets (levelled camera, ground 8–20° below the horizon, all
azimuths, no road mask; `make vigor-depth-height`, job 8855542, `depth_check/vigor_height_check.json`):

| Dataset | Implied camera height (median) | Panoramas |
|---|---|---|
| VIGOR | 1.21 m (Chicago 1.23, New York 1.13, San Francisco 1.26, Seattle 1.20) | 1200 |
| Poznań | 1.04 m (road-only fore/aft rule: 1.05 m, `depth_check/height_check.json`) | 200 |

The Poznań rig is ~1.65–1.7 m, so UniK3D under-scales; it does so on VIGOR too, and PanoRoMa was trained with that bias.
Rescaling Poznań to the true height (×1.6) would move it away from the training distribution; the consistent
correction is ×1.21/1.04 ≈ 1.16. Mismatch between the datasets ≈ 14 %. Together with the null `sim` solver result, depth
scale is at most a small factor. No rescale applied.

## Fixes made on the way (review of the three-way branch)

- FG² camera position is −Rᵀt (FG²'s solver maps satellite → ground); the old −t was right only at zero rotation.
- Loc²'s yaw sign is opposite to FG²'s; both pinned by planted-pose tests.
- PanoRoMa entries that fail are scored as misses instead of being dropped.
